test_harness.kind: Public-API behavior test in frame/airdrop/tests/oracle.rs. It builds a minimal FRAME mock runtime (frame_system + pallet_balances + pallet_timestamp + pallet_airdrop) with sp_io::TestExternalities and drives the pallet's public claim dispatchable (Airdrop::claim) with Origin::none() and an invalid Ethereum ownership proof Proof::Ethereum(EcdsaSignature([0u8;65])). At the start commit claim immediately routes the proof through Pallet::get_remote_account -> ethereum_recover (the deleted OLD production lines in frame/airdrop/src/lib.rs, including the sp_io::crypto::secp256k1_ecdsa_recover call), before any airdrop/association lookup; at the target commit those helpers are relocated into composable-support::signature_verification. The test asserts only observable behavior: an invalid proof is rejected (claim returns Err). It is solution-independent and passes on both the start and the source-only golden trees. The source_paths overlay relocates the reviewed helpers and the supporting composable-support abstractions refactor (an unrelated file->directory restructure that target airdrop lib.rs depends on) so the target production compiles against the start Cargo.lock; runtime/dali/Cargo.toml and composable-traits/src/lib.rs are deliberately excluded from the overlay because they pull in unrelated target-only workspace members (frame/ibc-transfer) and an unrelated staking/nft module set that are not part of the reviewed change. Coverage is collected on the start tree with cargo-llvm-cov over the same -p pallet-airdrop --test oracle invocation and executes the deleted OLD ethereum_recover / get_remote_account lines.

test_harness.kind: Public-API behavior test in demo-circuit/tests/oracle.rs. It builds the key-rotation setup circuit via the public NaiveThresholdSignatureWKeyRotation::get_instance_for_setup and indexes it with the public CoboundaryMarlin SNARK (type_mapping re-export). Indexing drives the circuit's ConstraintSynthesizer::generate_constraints, whose body lives in naive_threshold_sig_w_key_rotation/mod.rs at the start commit and is relocated into a constraints submodule at the target commit, so the test executes hundreds of deleted OLD locality lines while asserting only observable behavior (num_constraints > 0). demo-circuit/Cargo.toml is byte-identical at start and target, and target production compiles against the start Cargo.lock dependency graph, so the same test passes on both the start and the source-only golden trees. Coverage is collected on the start tree with cargo-llvm-cov over the same -p demo-circuit --test oracle invocation.

test_harness.kind: session behavior test through the public cargo-contract CLI. Running `cargo-contract contract instantiate --suri //Alice --salt 0x00 /nonexistent.contract` parses the `--salt` argument through the reviewed contract-extrinsics::instantiate value_parser `parse_hex_bytes` (crates/extrinsics/src/instantiate.rs), executing the deleted OLD lines of that helper during clap argument parsing, entirely offline and before any node connection. It then fails fast loading the missing .contract metadata file (exit 1, `Failed to open metadata file /nonexistent.contract`). At the target commit `parse_hex_bytes` and the whole clap `InstantiateCommand` were moved/rewritten (the extrinsics crate keeps only a plain `InstantiateOpts` and the CLI struct lives in cargo-contract/src/cmd/instantiate.rs), yet the same CLI still parses `--salt 0x00` and fails identically on the missing artifact. Observable behavior (non-zero exit + metadata error) is stable across start and target. Coverage is collected with a whole-workspace llvm-cov report (two-step --no-report test then report) so the contract-extrinsics dependency crate that owns the locality appears in the JSON.
